articles.title: AlpineBSD combines NetBSD with Alpine’s apk package manager
articles.summary: AlpineBSD uses the NetBSD kernel, libc, and essential tools, and combines them with Alpine’s apk-tools package manager, busybox, and generlaly preferring GNU tools over their BSD equivalents.

articles.title: Check out the demo for INANIMA, a retro survival-horror inspired by Resident Evil and SIGNALIS
articles.summary: INANIMA is an upcoming release from developer Obscure Tales (Lamentum) focused on you surviving in an isolated facility of a strange corporation. The developer emailed GamingOnLinux to note the new demo is live, with full Native Linux support.

articles.title: Claude Code v2.1.314
articles.summary: Added an optional groups list to Claude apps gateway upstreams: only developers in the listed IdP groups are sent to that upstream, on failover too.

articles.title: Where Did All the iPhone Duos Go? Mostly to Apple's Stores
articles.summary: Apple allocated roughly 80% of its initial iPhone Duo inventory to its retail stores, with locations holding as few as 50 units each, according to Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman.

articles.title: Apple’s best MacBook Pro decision this week had nothing to do with touch
articles.summary: Apple’s new touchscreen MacBook Pro brings plenty of welcome upgrades, but one of the best things about this week’s launch is what the company decided not to change.

articles.title: Latest Gemini design comes to all Android devices, app upgrades file generation
articles.summary: This updated design was first introduced on phones with Gemini Intelligence (Pixel 11) and is now available on all other devices we checked today. Make sure to Force stop the Google app if you’re not seeing it yet.

articles.title: Open source evolution sim 'Thrive' v1.7 works towards completing the multicellular stage
articles.summary: The multicellular stage is getting more complete for the open source evolution sim Thrive, with version 1.7 out now. Thrive is free and open source but you can buy it from stores to support the development.

articles.title: Mistral releases weights for its trillion-parameter AI model, targeting cybersecurity
articles.summary: French AI company Mistral has released the weights for its trillion-parameter open source AI model Mistral Large 4 (ML4), allowing businesses and governments to download and deploy the system themselves.

articles.title: Here’s everything new in Android 17 QPR3 Beta 3 [Gallery]
articles.summary: Over the coming hours, we’ll dive into all of Android 17 QPR3 Beta 3’s new features and every single change. (The newest updates will be at the top of this list.

articles.title: Dune: Awakening's free Blood and Ice expansion launches December 1
articles.summary: Funcom reveals the Blood and Ice expansion and detailed what's coming over the next three to four months - including new events, offline single-player and more.

articles.title: Paris-based Mistral releases "Le Chonk," a strong coding model that still trails China overall
articles.summary: Mistral has released the weights for Mistral Large 4, its largest model yet. The company says the model beats its open rivals at coding. In the first independent test, it turns out to be fast and fairly cheap, but it trails Chinese models in the overall rankings.

articles.title: Android 17 QPR3 Beta 3 rolling out with 26 Pixel fixes
articles.summary: Report issues via the Android Beta Feedback app on Pixel devices. Access it from the application drawer or Quick Settings to file bugs in Google’s issue tracker.

articles.title: Multiplayer music playground 'Vibe Together' sounds like a super-fun idea
articles.summary: “My two biggest loves are music and indie games. Vibe Together was born by bringing those two loves together: a place where music making feels more like playing a game,” said The Music Unc.

articles.title: iOS 27.2 adds new video feature that’s perfect for iPhone Duo
articles.summary: iOS 27.2 launched this week with many new features , including an upgrade for the Apple TV app that’s especially perfect for iPhone Duo: Multiview.

articles.title: Apple says it’s ‘only getting started’ updating macOS for touchscreens
articles.summary: Apple’s new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display ( pre-order here ) includes a variety of software optimizations for touch input. But Apple says it’s “only getting started” making macOS more touch-friendly.

articles.title: Adjustments to the Taiwan storefront of the App Store on iOS and iPadOS
articles.summary: As of October 31, 2026, the commission rate for standard Apple In-App Purchase and paid app transactions will be 26% on the Taiwan storefront of the App Store on iOS and iPadOS.

articles.title: LRMoE: Demand-Side Load Re-Calibration for Efficient MoE Training on Memory-Constrained Nodes
articles.summary: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models offer scalable capacity for Web applications, but uneven routing creates computation and communication bottlenecks. Existing placement and replication methods redistribute this workload, yet additional expert copies compete with token-related buffers for limited GPU memory.

articles.title: iOS 27.2 gives Shortcuts app these new and improved features
articles.summary: iOS 27.2 launched this week with a variety of new features for Siri AI , FaceTime , Messages , and more, plus a handful of improvements for the Shortcuts app.

articles.title: Amortized Localized Posterior Inference for Model Calibration with Application to an Ocean Turbulence Closure
articles.summary: Model discrepancy may prevent a single calibration parameter from reproducing a physical response across the context domain. In addition, uncertainties in observations and contexts affect calibration and must be accounted for and quantified.

articles.title: ThinkJev: One Thought, Every Budget for Calibrated Typed Decisions
articles.summary: Many uses of language models end in a typed decision: a choice among a closed set of options, whose probabilities code can act on. Reading those probabilities from one forward pass is fast but often wrong on decisions that take several steps, such as arithmetic, counting, and date comparison.

articles.title: Build shared workflows for your team with Copilot Automations
articles.summary: With Copilot Automations, you can combine prompts, triggers, and tools to design workflows around the way your team works. Copilot runs autonomously in the cloud, using only the tools you’ve allowed.

articles.title: OpenFrontiers: A Collection of Open Research Problems and a Benchmark for Scientific Rediscovery
articles.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have shown increasing promise in research-level problem solving, yet a comprehensive collection of such problems is still missing, and evaluating them on research-level problems remains challenging.

articles.title: Repository plugin defaults and enterprise plugin controls generally available
articles.summary: Repository plugin defaults and enterprise-managed plugin controls are now generally available in VS Code, Copilot CLI, and the GitHub Copilot app. Trusted repositories can install and enable default plugins for contributors.

articles.title: Generate and edit images directly in Copilot
articles.summary: You can now generate and edit images using natural language in GitHub Copilot. When you ask for an image, your selected reasoning model calls a dedicated image-generation tool powered by GPT Image 2.5 Flare, previews the result inline, and saves it to your project.

articles.title: How macOS Adapts Its Controls for Touch on the New MacBook Pro
articles.summary: Apple announced a new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display on Wednesday. It's Apple's first Mac with a screen that supports touch, and demonstrations Apple gave to the media show how macOS reshapes its controls for finger input.

articles.title: This app lets you manage Nothing & CMF earbuds on Linux
articles.summary: EarA , a new open-source tool, aims to nix that palaver. It’s a GTK4 app (with a CLI for those who prefer the terminal), and lets you change settings on earbuds like the Nothing Ear (a) and CMF Buds 2 , from your Linux desktop.

articles.title: Gelly is a GTK desktop music player for Jellyfin and Navidrome
articles.summary: If you run your own music streaming server using Jellyfin or Navidrome/Subsonic, and you want a solid desktop player to browse and stream your library in, Gelly is worth a look.

articles.title: Graphics/NPU Driver Changes Already Begin Queuing Up For What Will Be Linux 7.5
articles.summary: Since last week drm-misc-next pull requests have already been sent out to DRM-Next to begin staging new feature code for what's intended for the Linux 7.5 kernel cycle kicking off at the end of the year.
